hook: $19.99 trick that makes my entryway match my tree

scenes.visual_prompt: A fully decorated 7.5-foot tree in the living room, camera pans to a bare entry table nearby
scenes.on_screen_text: My tree was styled. My entryway wasn't.
scenes.voiceover: My living room tree looked great. My entryway table looked like an afterthought.

scenes.visual_prompt: PEIDUO 2ft birch tree with built-in warm-white LED lights on an entry table, price tag $19.99 visible
scenes.voiceover: I grabbed a $19.99 birch accent tree that already has warm-white LEDs built into the branches — no separate light layer needed.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hands applying leftover velvet ribbon and 2-3 ornament clusters from the same bundle onto the small birch tree
scenes.voiceover: I used the leftover ribbon and a couple of ornament clusters from the same $34 bundle I already bought for the big tree.

scenes.visual_prompt: Side-by-side of the mismatched-color accent tree scenario vs. the matching-palette accent tree scenario
scenes.on_screen_text: Mismatched = two decisions. Matched = one plan.
scenes.voiceover: A mismatched accent tree in different colors reads as two separate decorating decisions. Repeating the same palette reads as one plan.

scenes.visual_prompt: Wide shot showing both the living room tree and entryway accent tree in the same frame, same color palette
scenes.voiceover: Since most of the bundle's already used on the big tree, this second surface cost me under $5 in extra material.

scenes.visual_prompt: Text card with blog link graphic
scenes.on_screen_text: Full cost breakdown on the blog

caption: Boutique stagers don't rely on one expensive piece — they repeat the same 2-3 colors across every surface in a room. Here's how I stretched a $34 bundle into a second styled spot for under $5 more.
